```plato
//==
// # Noise
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Noise — the shared lattice vocabulary
//  - Basis noise evaluation
//  - Fractal noise evaluation
//  - Warped and derived noise evaluation

library Noise
{
    //==
    // # Noise — the shared lattice vocabulary
    //
    // The hashing and lattice-gradient primitives every noise field in
    // the basis, fractal and warped sections are written against. Nothing
    // here is a field itself: these are the deterministic pseudo-random building
    // blocks, kept in one place so that two noises given the same Seed and the same
    // lattice cell agree.
    //
    // The pseudo-randomness is integer hashing, not a random number generator: there
    // is no state, and `LatticeHash(seed, i, j)` is a pure function of its three
    // arguments. The exact constants are NOT part of the contract — values will
    // differ between library versions — but within one version every backend must
    // agree, which is why the mixing is written in whole-number arithmetic that
    // wraps rather than in floating point.
    //
    // Convention: Frequency scales the input domain, so a lattice cell is
    // 1 / Frequency wide, and higher frequency means smaller features. Scalar noises
    // range over [-1, 1] unless a doc comment says otherwise.

    //==
    // # Integer hashing

    // A whole-number avalanche mix: one bit of input changes about half the
    // output bits. The xor-shift-multiply shape of the Murmur3 finalizer. The
    // multiplications are expected to wrap.
    NoiseMix(x: Integer): Integer {
        var h1 = x.BitwiseXor(x.ShiftRight(15)) * 668265261;
        var h2 = h1.BitwiseXor(h1.ShiftRight(13)) * 374761393;
        return h2.BitwiseXor(h2.ShiftRight(16));
    }
```
